correctness.rationale: The source proves that type preservation is equivalent to having at least one unit multiplier in every active CRT component. Each degree-\(d_i\) component has \(4^{d_i}\) elements and exactly \(2^{d_i}\) nonunits. Thus an active component has \(4^{\ell d_i}-2^{\ell d_i}\) successful ordered local tuples, while an inactive component is unrestricted. CRT independence gives the product formula. The joint-coprimality count is the same product over all factors. Exhaustive enumeration of every multiplier tuple for the source's \(m=3\) examples at \(\ell=1,2,3\) verifies all formulas.

value.rationale: The primary paper uses its new criterion to drive systematic searches that produced 36 improved codes. The exact product law measures the viable search space before any distance computation and quantifies the gain from using the necessary-and-sufficient active-factor criterion instead of the simpler sufficient test. It also shows that seed valuation type is irrelevant to search density once the active factor degrees are known, giving a reusable planning invariant for future QC searches.
